headline: High: ChatGPT Desktop can ingest files/screenshots/clipboard while LightAgent has broad network and MCP access, creating default-path leakage and prompt-injection risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop reads files, screenshots, clipboard, and connected-app content, so it can ingest attacker-controlled text if LightAgent outputs are copied or surfaced there. LightAgent exposes MCP/stdin-stdout and tool-calling, so malformed content could be propagated into tool workflows. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than proven.
conditions: IF LightAgent output is copied into ChatGPT Desktop or a connected app, prompt-like instructions can be ingested.
IF ChatGPT Desktop treats imported file or clipboard content as trusted instructions, injected directives may be followed.
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the agents.
Require a human to sanitize LightAgent output before pasting into ChatGPT Desktop.
Use a separate workspace for any content passed from LightAgent to ChatGPT Desktop.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to all inter-agent content.
requires-engineering: enforce instruction/data separation in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code, while LightAgent handles conversations, memory, tool results, and secrets like api_key/tot_api_key. LightAgent’s broad egress and MCP/tooling increase the chance that sensitive material from ChatGPT Desktop is forwarded outward. The pair lacks documented isolation, so leakage risk is substantial.
conditions: IF ChatGPT Desktop receives sensitive uploads or screenshots and LightAgent later ingests them, those data can flow into LightAgent memory or tool results.
IF LightAgent forwards its context or tool results over broad egress, sensitive content may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets or regulated data in ChatGPT Desktop when LightAgent is in the workflow.
Turn off or minimize LightAgent memory for shared tasks.
Use separate accounts/API keys for each agent.
Review and redact outputs before any cross-agent transfer.
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction on LightAgent egress.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop has read-only filesystem access plus clipboard/screen capture, while LightAgent has broad network egress, browsers, subprocesses, and MCP. They do not both show unrestricted filesystem write, so the high-severity shared-write indicator is not met. Still, overlapping authority over the same workflow can conflict when LightAgent mutates remote state while ChatGPT Desktop reads or summarizes it.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external workflow state or MCP-backed resource, conflicting updates can occur.
IF LightAgent subprocesses modify artifacts that ChatGPT Desktop is simultaneously reading, stale or inconsistent state may result.
mitigations: Assign one agent as read-only reviewer.
Separate writable resources by agent.
Pause one agent before the other edits shared artifacts.
Use explicit version checks before accepting updates.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared workflow state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can consume files, screenshots, and connected-app content, so LightAgent outputs can become inputs without a guaranteed verification step. LightAgent also emits tool results and provenance metadata, which may be treated as authoritative by downstream consumers. The pair therefore supports an error cascade, though not an automatic action-taking chain.
conditions: IF LightAgent-generated summaries are pasted or routed into ChatGPT Desktop without verification, errors can propagate.
IF ChatGPT Desktop is used to draft decisions from LightAgent outputs, mistaken facts may be amplified.
mitigations: Require a second-pass human check on LightAgent outputs.
Ask ChatGPT Desktop to cite source artifacts before acting on summaries.
Keep raw tool results separate from synthesized conclusions.
Use a checklist for any downstream decision based on either agent.
requires-engineering: add automated provenance verification.

E_compliance.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop handles uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code under OpenAI-managed services, while LightAgent handles conversations, memory, tool results, and secrets with broad egress. The profiles do not specify matching residency, retention, or DPA terms, so compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed by both agents under different retention or residency terms, a policy mismatch exists.
IF EU or PHI data is routed through LightAgent without a matching agreement, compliance exposure increases.
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to either agent.
Keep regulated data out of mixed-agent workflows.
Confirm residency and retention terms for both vendors.
Document a single approved data path for sensitive classes.
requires-engineering: obtain legal/compliance review for cross-agent processing.
